newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche Telekom shares seen well below 30 marks.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Telekom shares seen well below 30 marks.

text.p: Wheeling and dealing over the price for shares in Deutsche Telekom AG will turn white-hot next week when the company sets the price range for institutional investors in Europe's largest-ever flotation.

But despite overwhelming interest in the issue by private investors, fund managers and industry analysts say the risks are high and the share price will probably be well below the 30 German mark ($19.50) target the company had hoped to gain.

When Telekom unveils its final sales prospectus on Monday, investors are expecting the company to set a range of 23 marks ($14.95) to 29 marks ($18.85) as it begins taking bids from investors on Tuesday.

"The fair value for us is around 23 marks to 24 marks, but that's likely to be the lower end of the range," Michael Makris, fund manager at Oppenheim Kapitalanlagen GmbH, said on Friday. "The initial offering price will probably be in the upper mid-20s."
Investors will have from Oct. 22 until Nov. 14 to place orders for some of the 500 million shares that Telekom will list on stock exchanges in Germany, New York and Tokyo.
The final price for the shares will be set during the weekend of Nov. 16 and 17 and trade in the shares begins on Nov. 18 in Europe and the United States and a day later in Japan.
